title: What Is Nunchi? The Korean Art of Reading the Room
html:
Watch a K-drama long enough and someone will scold another character for having "no nunchi." There is no single English word for it, which is exactly why nunchi (눈치) has started appearing in English articles and self-help books.

In one line

Nunchi is the ability to sense what other people are thinking and feeling, without being told, and to act accordingly. In English we would say "reading the room."

Where the word comes from

Nun (눈) is the native Korean word for "eye." The word is often translated literally as "eye-measure," the idea of sizing up a situation with your eyes. According to Wikipedia, it first appears in 17th-century writing as nunch'ŭi, written with the characters 眼勢, roughly "eye force." The exact origin of the second syllable is not settled, so treat neat etymologies you see online with some caution.

How Koreans use it

  • Nunchi-ga ppareuda (눈치가 빠르다): "has quick nunchi," picks up on things fast.
  • Nunchi-ga itda (눈치가 있다): "has nunchi," socially sharp.
  • Nunchi-ga eopda (눈치가 없다): "has no nunchi," socially clumsy. This is the one you hear in dramas.
  • Nunchi-reul boda (눈치를 보다): "to watch someone's nunchi," to be careful about how someone will react, sometimes nervously. Leaving work before your boss does? You might be "watching nunchi."

In the news

In an October 17, 2026 column, The Korea Times argued that nunchi has two sides. It helps people be considerate and keeps a classroom or office running smoothly, but it can also push people to conform and leave those who miss the signals feeling excluded. The writer links Korea's habit of nonverbal communication to Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian traditions and compares nunchi with another famous Korean trait, ppalli-ppalli ("hurry, hurry").

The idea also travelled abroad through Euny Hong's 2019 book The Power of Nunchi, which presented it as a social skill anyone can practise.

Don't confuse it with

  • Empathy: feeling with someone. Nunchi is more about noticing and responding quickly, even if you do not share the feeling.
  • Kibun (기분): a person's mood or feelings. Good nunchi means protecting someone's kibun.
  • Jeong (정): a deep feeling of attachment that builds over time. Nunchi is moment to moment.

Sources

  • Wikipedia: Nunchi
  • The Korea Times: 'Nunchi' levels up (Oct 17, 2026)
  • World Economic Forum: The power of nunchi, an extract from Euny Hong's book (2019)
